tier: Tokyo zone So-Net Standard, Pro, Extreme and Unlimited

free_tier.stated: No free tier. So-Net Standard is JPY 8,800 a month: 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 30 GB HDD, 1 Tokyo-zone IPv4, 10240 GiB transfer, 200 Mbps port. So-Net Pro is JPY 12,800 a month (4 GB RAM, 50 GB, 15360 GiB, 300 Mbps) and the Unlimited plan is JPY 25,800 a month with unlimited transfer at a 300 Mbps port. All displayed prices are stated as tax included.
free_tier.notes: Prices are in Japanese yen as the vendor prints them. The cart showed stock counts beside each So-Net plan (5, 14, 10 and 1 available).

retention.stated: not applicable: a rented machine and its address, not stored bytes. The terms on non-payment are unverified: the cart and home page state none.

egress.terms: Transfer is allowed per month in GiB per plan: 10240 GiB on So-Net Standard, 15360 GiB on So-Net Pro, 30720 GiB on Extreme, unlimited on the Unlimited plan. No overage price is stated. Each plan also carries a notice that BitTorrent and banking-web use is banned.
egress.free_allowance: 10240 GiB per month on So-Net Standard; unlimited on So-Net Unlimited

interface_detail: A virtual server with one fixed Tokyo-zone IPv4 address. The access method (SSH or RDP) is not stated on the cart or home page; the vendor describes a self-service console.
tooling: An SSH or RDP client, whichever the image supports, plus a proxy or tunnel daemon the user installs on the machine. The vendor publishes no proxy endpoint and no API on the pages read.
chaining: A Worker opens an outbound connection to the server's fixed IPv4 and the server makes the upstream request, so the upstream sees an address in the So-Net or KDDI network the plan names instead of AS13335.

limits.value: 10240 GiB per month on So-Net Standard, 15360 GiB on So-Net Pro; unlimited on So-Net Unlimited

limits_note: The vendor's own pages sell a Tokyo-zone So-Net or KDDI address and do not use the word residential. The double-ISP residential label comes from a third-party review. No test address is published on the pages read, so no registry lookup was possible.
binding_note: The smallest monthly allowance, 10240 GiB, is far above a low-volume exit, so no quota binds. What decides the record is the registration class of the delivered address, which is unverified.

identity_cost.detail: The registration form asks for family name, given name, email address, phone number, city and postal code and a captcha; only the company name is marked optional. The form as read stops before the payment step, so any identity check at payment is unverified. A review states payment by credit card and Alipay.

reliability_note: Stock is shown per plan, with one So-Net Unlimited unit available when read. Bandwidth peaks are port rates; the review sites report the plan names but this record holds no measurement of delivered throughput.
confidence_note: Prices, allowances and the registration form fields are documented from the vendor's cart and registration page. That the addresses are residential or double-ISP is reported by a third-party review and is unverified here. Nothing was measured.
